notes: Net spend is -15.8% against a ~-30% target, and the gap has two stated causes rather than one unknown. (1) Only 59 of 200 requests routed cheap, because 57% of this seeded set is Rs.10,000+ traffic that the stakes threshold forces to the strong tier -- a corpus artefact, not a router failure. (2) No cache hit is modelled at all; the plan's conservative 20-45% range is deliberately not claimed because nothing in this build has measured one.
Generation is held fixed across both arms: identical model output, so every difference is Interlock's. Generation latency and billing are NOT observed.

NOTHING passes above Rs.10,000. That is the objective working, not failing: at Rs.40,000 impact with a 2.5x reversibility multiplier, L0_pass only wins if P(defect) < ~0.0001. The detector's floor on clean text is ~0.02, so high-stakes traffic cannot pass at any detector quality short of ~1-in-10,000 false positives. Finding F-019 -- this is a question about the impact model, not about the detector.
